headline: High-risk pairwise mismatch: EMQX’s broad HTTP egress can exfiltrate data while the other profile is a non-runnable docs-only list with no protective runtime boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. agent_a is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, while agent_b is EMQX with HTTP API and broad egress; there is no shared channel or parser path shown that would let one agent’s output steer the other as instructions.
conditions: IF a shared clipboard, filesystem, or MCP bridge is added between the pair, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a begins emitting machine-readable instructions consumed by agent_b, the severity increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future shared MCP or message-queue bridge.
Require explicit provenance tags on any text passed between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A leakage pathway exists because agent_b has broad network egress and an HTTP API, while agent_a is a docs-only repository with no declared data classes. The pair does not show a shared workspace, so this is not high; however, if agent_a content or operator data is forwarded into agent_b, EMQX can transmit it outward.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded into agent_b inputs, then those contents can leave the local boundary via HTTP.
IF either agent is configured to process sensitive operator data, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or private documents from agent_a into agent_b.
Restrict agent_b egress with firewall rules.
Use a redaction step before any handoff.
Log outbound destinations for agent_b.
requires-engineering: add per-field data-loss prevention on the handoff.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, while agent_b exposes HTTP API and broad egress but no filesystem or git write capability is listed. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; uncertainty stays low because missing write surfaces are informative here.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk rises.
IF agent_b gains filesystem or git write permissions, reassess for concurrent mutation.
mitigations: Keep mutable resources single-writer.
Avoid sharing a writable workspace.
Document ownership of any API targets.
Use locks if a shared resource is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error pathway exists if agent_b treats agent_a’s outputs as authoritative. agent_a is a curated list with no runtime verification, and agent_b can act over HTTP; if agent_a-derived content is forwarded into EMQX workflows without checks, downstream actions may be triggered on unverified material.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a output without a verification step, then erroneous content can propagate downstream.
IF agent_b is configured to trigger external actions from received messages, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step.
Mark agent_a output as untrusted by default.
Require schema validation before agent_b acts.
Limit agent_b to read-only processing for handoffs.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware gating.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b touches IoT data, so the only compliance concern is a generic one: if regulated IoT data is routed through EMQX, policy review is needed. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because none is shown.
conditions: IF regulated IoT data is routed through agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency requirements are imposed on the shared data flow, reassess severity.
mitigations: Classify the IoT data before routing.
Confirm retention settings for agent_b.
Restrict agent_b to approved regions.
Record the data-processing purpose.
requires-engineering: add residency enforcement.
